test_title: PYST 24: SSC CHSL - English (Held On: 16 March, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: english
question:
Some parts of a few sentences have been jumbled up, and labelled A, B, C and D. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

I knew that the remedy lay not

A. let the past go. Be at ease. Allow the future

B. Rohan had advised me over and again:

C. to arrive at its own pace

D. in finding a new flower but in what unfurling its secrets when it will.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1' **i.e. **'DBAC'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **correct sequence** is indeed:** DBAC**
 
• **Rearranging the sentence** parts according to this sequence gives us a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence:
 
• "I knew that the remedy lay not in finding a new flower but in what unfurling its secrets when it will **(D)** Rohan had advised me over and again **(B)**: let the past go. Be at ease. Allow the future **(A)** to arrive at its own pace **(C)."**
 
• So, the correct sequence is **DBAC**,** creating a coherent narrative** where the speaker reflects on Rohan's advice as the remedy they were looking for.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: **'DBAC'.**
